What arrives is usually a push rather than an invitation: a demand, a challenge, an opening that requires you to move before you have finished deliberating. Whatever you begin now carries the mark of the choice you make between the two ends of this axis — the practised manoeuvre, or the unfamiliar effort. Both will present themselves as necessary. Only one of them takes you anywhere new. This happens once and not again for nearly nineteen years.
node-conjunction-jupiter: The node reaches your Jupiter, and the line of your development crosses your capacity for growth. What arrives tends to be an enlargement: an opportunity, a door held open, a piece of good fortune roughly in the direction you were supposed to be walking. Jupiter makes both ends of this axis look inviting, which is the difficulty — the flattering opportunity and the necessary one are equally attractive now. Take the one you are not yet good at. Contacts of this generosity come once and do not return for nearly nineteen years.
node-conjunction-saturn: The node reaches your Saturn, and the direction of your life crosses its structure. What arrives here is concrete and costs something: a commitment taken on, a responsibility accepted, a place settled into that closes the easier options. It will not feel expansive. What it establishes is the framework inside which the actual development happens, and frameworks of this kind get built once and then lived in for a long time. This crossing comes round only every nineteen years or so; what you agree to now, you will be inside for much of that.
node-conjunction-uranus: The node reaches your Uranus, and your own direction crosses the part of you that wants out. What arrives comes from an angle you were not watching — a person outside your usual circle, an idea from another field, a chance that does not resemble the ones you had been waiting for. Because it does not match the plan, it is easy to dismiss on exactly those grounds. Novelty is not a sufficient reason to act and it is a good reason to look. This crosses once and not again for nearly nineteen years.
node-conjunction-neptune: The node reaches your Neptune, and the line of your development crosses the dissolving principle. What arrives is rarely an event; it is more often an intuition of direction that you could not argue for and cannot quite dismiss — a sense of which way is forward, without any schedule attached. It is easy to talk yourself out of afterwards, so it is worth recording while it is legible. Neptune supplies no plans. What it does supply here is orientation, and orientation of this kind comes round about once every nineteen years.
node-conjunction-pluto: The node reaches your Pluto, and the direction of your life crosses the regenerating principle. What comes is rarely gentle: something has to be given up before the way forward is visible, and the removal generally precedes the direction rather than following it. Attachments loosen, a role stops satisfying, and what remains is clearer for the absence. Pluto is impersonal and does not negotiate. This crossing happens once and not again for nearly nineteen years, and its consequences take considerably longer than that to work out.
node-conjunction-node: Your nodal return, at roughly nineteen, thirty-seven, fifty-six and seventy-four. The whole axis of your direction comes back to its own place, closing a cycle and opening another. At nineteen it marks the passage into adult life; at thirty-seven, a reckoning with what the first full cycle actually produced; at fifty-six, the question of what the rest is for. Rudhyar's terms hold at each: progress along this line is made by exertion, and habit is established at the other end by repetition. Which of the two the last cycle mostly consisted of becomes visible now.
node-conjunction-chiron: The node reaches your Chiron, and the line of your development crosses the old injury — a pairing with more in it than is obvious, since very often the work you are here to do runs directly through the place where you were damaged. That connection surfaces now. What is wanted is not the competence you already have but the thing you understand because it cost you something, which is an uncomfortable qualification and the genuine one. This crosses once and not again for nearly nineteen years. Notice how closely what is being asked resembles what you have been avoiding.
node-conjunction-mc: The node reaches the highest point of your chart, and the line of your development crosses your public standing. What arrives usually arrives through work or reputation: an offer, a role, a visibility that turns out to be pointing somewhere. The practised competence at the far end of this axis is exactly what is easiest to be recognised for, which is the difficulty — the recognition on offer may be for the version of yourself you have already outgrown. Take what advances the harder direction. This crosses once and not again for nearly nineteen years.
chiron-conjunction-sun: Chiron crosses the centre, and what it touches is the relationship between who you are and where you were damaged. Something exposes the gap: a situation in which your ordinary confidence simply is not available, or a role you cannot occupy without the old injury showing. That is uncomfortable and it is the point. Chiron's wound in the myth could not be healed and could not be escaped, and what the centaur did with it was teach. This is the angle at which the same conversion becomes possible for you — not the injury cured, but the injury made into something you can offer.
chiron-sextile-sun: A workable, undramatic contact between your sense of yourself and your oldest sore spot. Usually it arrives as an opportunity: somebody needs the particular understanding that only your own history could have given you, or somebody offers you help in a form you can actually accept. Both are the same transit and either is worth taking. Nothing insists, and because nothing insists, the whole passage often goes by unremarked. What is briefly available is the ability to be who you are without first having to conceal the part that was hurt.
chiron-square-sun: Something presses directly on the wound where it touches your identity, and the reaction will run larger than the occasion warrants. Often it takes the form of being unable to occupy your own position — a role you cannot inhabit, a confidence that deserts you exactly when needed, a comparison you cannot stop making. Both easy responses are worth avoiding: insisting nothing landed, and settling into the injury as a description of yourself, which is more comfortable than it looks. What is being asked is whether the thing can be made useful rather than either denied or inhabited.
chiron-trine-sun: A rare interval in which you can look at the old damage without flinching and without it costing you your footing. Nothing is pressing on it; it is simply legible, and you are recognisably yourself while looking. That combination makes this a good period for saying something you normally go around, for taking on work in the territory where you were hurt, or for being genuinely useful to someone in the same difficulty. Chiron does not heal; what it does is become teachable. Here the conversion costs least, and what is understood tends to hold.
chiron-opposition-sun: You meet the injury in someone else, and it is aimed at your sense of who you are. Somebody arrives carrying openly what you carry quietly — a rival, a mentor, a casualty, sometimes all three — and the encounter puts your own vulnerability where you cannot avoid looking at it. You can treat their trouble as entirely theirs and stay outside it, or recognise the shape. The second is harder and much more useful. What you find yourself able to say to them is usually the thing you have never managed to say to yourself.
chiron-conjunction-moon: Chiron crosses the region of instinct and belonging, and the material that surfaces is old — early, familial, formed before you could examine it. Something touches the place where nurture failed or came with conditions, and the response arrives at full childhood volume. That disproportion is the useful signal rather than an embarrassment. What becomes possible here is looking after somebody else in exactly the way you were not looked after, which is Chiron's characteristic conversion and is not the same as repeating the injury from the other side. The distinction matters and is worth watching.
chiron-sextile-moon: A gentle contact with the oldest sore place, arriving through feeling rather than event. Someone may need the kind of care your own history qualifies you to give, or offer you the same in a form you can finally take — which is usually the harder of the two, and is briefly easier now. Defences are down and nothing is pressing on them. It costs almost nothing to use, and it is easy to let pass. What is on offer is not repair but a temporary end to the effort of holding the thing at arm's length.
chiron-square-moon: Something presses on the injury where it lives in your instincts, and family or domestic life is usually the medium. An old pattern reactivates over something small; a need that was never met announces itself as irritation, or as a demand aimed at whoever happens to be nearest. The intensity is information about the wound rather than about the person in front of you. Both denial and immersion are available and neither is useful. What is being asked is whether the need can be stated plainly instead of acted out, which is unglamorous and is the whole work.
chiron-trine-moon: The old damage becomes bearable to feel. Nothing is inflamed and nothing is denied — it is simply present and can be looked at with some kindness, including toward yourself, which is the rarer half. That makes this a good interval for saying something to someone who would understand, or for offering the kind of care that only experience of the same trouble can supply. What Chiron does instead of healing is become usable, and this is the angle at which that conversion happens without cost. What is learned here tends to stay learned.
chiron-opposition-moon: You meet the injury through someone close, and it arrives at the level of need. Somebody wants from you exactly what you were never given, or gives you something you have never known how to accept. Either way the old deficit becomes visible because it is standing outside you wearing another face. The tempting responses are to supply endlessly from a well that was never filled, or to refuse on the grounds that nobody supplied you. Neither works. What does is recognising the shape and saying so, which is harder and considerably more use to both of you.
chiron-conjunction-mercury: Chiron crosses the way you think and speak, and finds the place where your own account of things is built around an injury. Something you have long said about yourself turns out to be a defence rather than a description. That is uncomfortable and it is also the opening: for a while you can put language to a thing you normally have no words for, which is precisely how a wound stops being merely damage. Chiron taught rather than healed, and articulacy is the beginning of teaching. If someone would understand, this is the period to tell them.
chiron-sextile-mercury: A light verbal contact with the sore place. Someone may say the useful thing, or ask you a question your own experience makes you able to answer properly. What is briefly available is the ability to talk about the injury without the usual armouring — the words are there and the defence is down simultaneously, which is rarer than it sounds. Nothing forces the issue, so it can easily go by unused. Writing something down works as well as saying it, and sometimes better, since it does not require anyone else to be ready.
chiron-square-mercury: Something said lands directly on the wound, or something you say does it to somebody else. The reaction outruns the cause by a wide margin. The two available responses are both worth resisting: flatly denying that anything landed, and reciting the grievance at length, which is more comfortable than it looks and settles nothing. What the angle asks is whether you can find words that describe the injury rather than defend it. Take the intensity as data about the wound and not as a verdict on the conversation, and hold off on conclusions until it passes.
chiron-trine-mercury: One of the rarer intervals in which the old damage can be described rather than defended. Nothing is pressing on it and the language is available, which makes this a good period for saying out loud something you normally route around, or for being genuinely useful to someone in the same difficulty. Your understanding is accurate and unforced. Chiron's contribution is never repair; it is the turn from suffering to teaching, and this is the angle at which that turn costs least. What is understood now tends to stay understood, having been arrived at without pressure.
chiron-opposition-mercury: You meet the injury in what somebody else says. Someone describes openly what you have kept private, or asks the question you have arranged your explanations to avoid. You can treat it as entirely their concern or recognise the shape. The second is harder and considerably more useful. Oppositions put a thing outside you where it can be examined, and this one hands you your own vulnerability in another person's words. What you find yourself saying back to them is very often the sentence you have never managed to say to yourself; note it afterwards.
chiron-conjunction-venus: Chiron crosses what you value and how you love, and finds the injury there. Something tender presses on something sore: an affection difficult to accept, a closeness that reactivates an older loss, a moment of being valued that shows how long you have gone without. The reaction may be larger than the occasion. What is available in exchange is an unusual gentleness toward damage — yours and other people's — and the capacity to offer exactly the kind of care your own history has qualified you for. Chiron does not close the wound; it changes what the wound is for.
chiron-sextile-venus: A soft contact with the sore place, usually arriving through somebody else. A person may offer you the sort of care that your particular injury makes hard to receive, or ask you for the kind only experience could have taught. Both are the same transit and either is worth taking. Defences are lower than usual and nothing is pressing on them, which is a combination that does not come round often. It costs little to use and is easy to let pass unremarked, which is generally what happens to it.
chiron-square-venus: Something in your attachments presses on the injury. Often the discovery is that you cannot quite receive what is being offered, or that what you want from someone is shaped by an old deficit rather than by them. The two easy responses are both worth resisting: pretending nothing landed, and settling into the ache as somewhere familiar to live. What the angle asks is whether the wound can be brought into the relationship as something spoken about rather than acted out. Take the intensity as information about the injury and not as a judgement on the person.
chiron-trine-venus: The old damage can be felt without defence and without enough pain to obscure it. Nothing presses; it is simply legible, and there is enough warmth around it to make looking bearable. That makes this a good moment to say something you normally go around, or to be useful to someone in the same trouble, since your sympathy is accurate and costs you nothing to give. Chiron's conversion is from injury into something offerable, and this is the angle at which it happens most cheaply. What is understood now generally holds.
chiron-opposition-venus: You meet the injury through someone you care about. They carry openly what you carry quietly, and the encounter can go two ways: you can treat their trouble as entirely theirs and stay comfortably outside it, or recognise the shape and admit it is familiar. The second is harder and much more useful. Affection makes the recognition possible and also makes it uncomfortable. What you find yourself able to say to them is usually the thing you have never managed to say to yourself. Remember it once the feeling has settled.
chiron-conjunction-mars: Chiron crosses the drive to assert yourself and finds the place where asserting yourself has cost you. Something strikes the injury and the response comes out as anger — faster and sharper than the situation warrants, because what is being defended is much older than what is in front of you. The other face of it is genuine fight on the wound's behalf: this is a characteristic angle for finally pushing back against something long absorbed, or for acting on behalf of somebody in the same position. Which you get depends on whether you can see what you are actually angry about.
chiron-sextile-mars: A workable opening onto the sore place, with enough energy behind it to act. Something can be done about it now rather than only felt — a step taken, a limit set, help offered to somebody whose trouble you recognise because it is also yours. Nothing is pressing hard enough to make you defensive, and the will to move is there at the same time, which is an unusual combination. Chiron's wound does not close; what it does is become the source of the help you are qualified to give. This is a cheap moment to act on that.
chiron-square-mars: Something presses on the injury and the response comes out as force: an argument, a refusal, an action taken fast enough that you do not have to feel what prompted it. Sometimes that is exactly right and long overdue. Sometimes it is flight dressed as decisiveness, and the wound travels with you. The question is whether what you are about to do addresses the thing or merely outruns it — both feel urgent, and urgency is not evidence either way. If there is a real fight to be had here, this supplies the nerve for it. Be sure you have the right opponent.
chiron-trine-mars: Strength and old damage occupy the same ground without conflict, which does not happen often. You can act from what has hurt you rather than around it: set a limit, say the difficult thing, take on the situation you have avoided precisely because it touched that place. Nothing is inflamed and nothing is denied. Your capacity to be useful to somebody in the same difficulty is at its most available and costs the least effort. What Chiron does instead of healing is become teachable, and this is where that conversion is easiest to make.
chiron-opposition-mars: You meet the injury in the middle of a conflict. Somebody carries openly what you carry quietly, and the collision can go two ways: you can fight them and treat the trouble as entirely theirs, or recognise the shape and see that the fight is not really with them. The second is harder and much more useful. Oppositions put a thing outside you where it can be looked at, and this one does it during an argument — a poor moment for insight and an excellent one for evidence. Note what you said. It usually applies to you.
chiron-conjunction-jupiter: Chiron reaches your capacity for meaning and enlarges the wound accordingly. Sometimes that means the injury is felt at full size for a while, more visible than it has been in years. More often it acquires a frame: you can see what it cost, what it taught, and what it lets you do for somebody else. This is a characteristic angle for taking up teaching, healing or advocacy in the exact territory where you were damaged. What is offered is meaning rather than repair, and meaning is what Chiron trades in — the centaur could not cure himself and taught the physicians.
chiron-sextile-jupiter: A generous, low-cost contact with the sore place. Something opens — a conversation, a book, a person, a chance to be useful — that lets you make something of the injury rather than merely carry it. Understanding is available and the defences are not up, which is not a common pairing. Somebody may need exactly what your history qualifies you to give, or offer you the same in a form you can finally accept. Nothing insists on any of it, which is why the moment usually passes without being noticed. It is worth using.
chiron-square-jupiter: The wound gets inflated, and the inflation is uncomfortable: what hurt you starts to look like the whole picture rather than part of it, or a conviction built on it turns into something you want to preach. Both are the same distortion. What the angle actually asks is whether you can make the injury useful without making it your entire philosophy — whether the meaning you draw from it survives contact with anything outside itself. Generosity offered from a wound is real and goes astray easily in the choosing. Watch who you are giving it to, and what you are getting back.
chiron-trine-jupiter: An unusually kind angle on old damage. Nothing presses on it, and enough perspective is available to see the shape whole — what it cost, what it taught, and what it lets you understand about other people. A good period for doing something with that: helping someone in the same difficulty, saying what you normally route around, or taking up the work your history has actually qualified you for. What is learned here holds, because it was learned with room rather than under pressure. Meaning arrived at this way tends to survive.
chiron-opposition-jupiter: You meet the injury in somebody else, magnified. Someone arrives carrying openly, and probably at volume, what you carry quietly — a teacher, a casualty, or both — and the encounter puts your own vulnerability where you have to look at it. Generosity is available and is the right response, provided it does not become a way of managing your own wound by attending to theirs. Watch for the impulse to instruct from a place you have not actually got past. What you find yourself telling them is usually addressed to you.
chiron-conjunction-saturn: Chiron reaches your sense of limit and structure, and the two have a great deal in common: both concern what cannot simply be wished away. What surfaces is the point where an old injury and a real constraint are the same thing — a limitation you have carried so long that you can no longer tell whether it is a fact about you or a habit. Sorting that out is the work, and it is slow. What Saturn contributes is form: the wound acquires edges, and something with edges can be planned around and eventually built on.
chiron-sextile-saturn: A practical, unspectacular contact with the sore place. Something can be built here rather than only felt: a discipline taken up, a limit formally accepted, a piece of work that grows directly out of what your own history taught you. There is enough detachment to look at the injury without being inside it and enough patience to do something slow about it. Nothing forces the issue and none of it will feel significant at the time. This is one of the intervals in which a wound quietly becomes a competence, entirely undramatically.
chiron-square-saturn: The injury meets structure and the structure presses on it. Often this arrives as a limitation formally imposed — a refusal, an obligation, a circumstance that will not accommodate you — landing precisely where you are least able to absorb it. The characteristic feeling is of being held to a standard your particular damage makes unreachable. Some of that is accurate; a good deal of it is the habit of grading yourself harshly. What is being asked is whether you can accept a genuine limit without turning it into a verdict on yourself. Those are different, and they feel identical now.
chiron-trine-saturn: The old damage sits in a solid frame and can be looked at steadily. Nothing presses on it, and there is enough perspective to see what it actually cost, what it taught, and what it makes you able to do. That combination is rare and worth using: a good interval for taking on work, formal or otherwise, in the exact territory where you were once hurt, because you can now do it without being run by it. Chiron does not heal; it becomes usable. Saturn's contribution is that what is built here lasts.
chiron-opposition-saturn: You meet the injury from outside, and it arrives dressed as authority, limitation or plain circumstance. Something says no exactly where you are least equipped to hear it, or somebody in a position of power over you touches the old place without knowing. The response worth avoiding is treating a real limit as proof of inadequacy; the other one worth avoiding is refusing to see the limit at all. Oppositions put a thing outside you where it can be examined. Examine it, and be more accurate than either the fear or the defiance would be.
chiron-conjunction-uranus: Chiron reaches the part of you that wants out, and jolts the injury. Something breaks open: a pattern that has held the wound in place for years suddenly gives, often through an abrupt event nobody planned. The characteristic experience is discovering that a limitation you accepted as permanent was actually a habit, which is exhilarating and destabilising in about equal measure. Chiron does not close; what can change is what it is allowed to determine. Sudden release from a long accommodation is the best form of this. Sudden exposure of what the accommodation concealed is the harder one.
chiron-sextile-uranus: An unexpected and inexpensive opening onto the sore place. Something arrives from outside the usual channels — an unfamiliar method, a person with no stake in your history, an idea that reframes what you had assumed was settled — and for a while the injury looks different from how it has always looked. Nothing forces the reappraisal, which is why it often passes unused. What is available is the willingness to try something new on a problem you had stopped expecting to solve. That pairing does not come round often.
chiron-square-uranus: Something abrupt presses on the injury, and the response is likely to be a break: a walk-out, a refusal, a change made fast enough that you do not have to feel what caused it. Sometimes that is exactly right and long overdue. Sometimes it is flight in the language of liberation, and the wound simply relocates. The angle asks whether the change addresses the injury or outruns it. Both feel urgent, and urgency settles nothing. What is genuinely intolerable will still be intolerable in a month, which is the only reliable test available.
chiron-trine-uranus: The old damage and the impulse to change agree, which lets you do something about it without breaking anything else. An unfamiliar approach becomes available — a method, a person, a way of framing the thing — and you are open enough to try it without the usual defensive reflex. A good period for taking up something genuinely new in the exact territory where you were hurt, since the wound is legible and the appetite for a different approach is real at the same moment. Chiron does not heal; here it becomes usable in an unexpected form.
chiron-opposition-uranus: The injury is jolted from outside. Someone or something arrives abruptly and touches the old place, breaking a pattern you had settled into around it — usually before you have decided whether you wanted it broken. The first response will be to get away from whoever delivered it. The more useful one is to notice what the shock actually revealed, which is generally an accommodation you had stopped recognising as one. Oppositions put a thing outside you where it can be examined; this one does it without warning, which is inconvenient and unusually clarifying.
chiron-conjunction-neptune: Chiron reaches the dissolving principle and the injury loses its outline. At best that means the wound stops being a hard particular thing and becomes something you can feel compassion about — in yourself and in everyone else — as the boundary between your damage and the general kind genuinely thins. At worst the same dissolution makes the injury impossible to locate: a diffuse sadness with no object, or an identification with suffering at large that quietly excuses you from your own. Both are available, and what separates them is whether the compassion has an address.
chiron-sextile-neptune: A gentle, permeable contact with the sore place. Sympathy is available — including, unusually, for yourself — and the defences that normally guard the area are simply not up. That makes this a good moment for anything contemplative aimed at the injury, and for accepting care that your particular damage usually makes hard to take. Nothing insists, and the whole passage can go by unnoticed. What is on offer is not repair; Chiron does not repair. It is a temporary suspension of the effort of holding the thing at a distance.
chiron-square-neptune: The defences around the injury dissolve at the wrong moment, and what surfaces is diffuse rather than specific: a general helplessness, a sense of being damaged in a way you cannot name or address. The temptation is to make it meaningful — to read the pain as a calling, to cast yourself as the one who suffers on everybody's behalf, to find in the wound a reason not to act. Watch what the suffering is buying you. Where it buys nothing, it is simply pain, and can be treated as such, which is a considerable relief.
chiron-trine-neptune: The old damage becomes permeable without becoming overwhelming. You can feel it without defending against it, and feel it in other people at the same time, which is the particular gift here: the wound stops being only yours. Good ground for any work where your own history is what qualifies you, and for the kind of quiet practice that changes your relationship to something rather than removing it. Chiron does not close; what alters is what it costs to carry. Here it costs less, and what you understand about it tends to last.
chiron-opposition-neptune: You meet the injury dissolved into somebody else. Someone arrives carrying, diffusely and often helplessly, what you carry precisely, and the boundary between their trouble and yours will be genuinely hard to find. That is the difficulty and the opportunity at once. Real compassion is available, and so is a complete loss of proportion in which you take on what is not yours and call it kindness. The test is whether you can be moved by someone without merging with them. Where you cannot, the help does neither of you any good.
chiron-conjunction-pluto: Chiron reaches the regenerating principle and the injury is excavated. What has been managed for years gets dug out: where it came from, what it cost, and the whole arrangement you built to live around it. This is not gentle and it is not gratuitous. Chiron's wound does not close, and what changes here is its position — it stops being the hidden centre of your arrangements and becomes something you have looked at squarely. The process is slow and its first half is largely descent. What gets rebuilt afterwards rests on something other than avoidance.
chiron-sextile-pluto: A slow, workable contact with the old injury, in which real depth becomes available without a crisis forcing it. Something loosens — a defence you no longer need, an account of the wound that turns out to be partial — and you can look further into it than usual without being overwhelmed. Unusually good ground for serious therapeutic work, or for taking on something in the territory where you were hurt. Nothing here compels you, which means it can go unused. What is on offer is depth without the cost that depth usually carries.
chiron-square-pluto: Pressure comes to bear on the injury and does not let up. Something in your circumstances keeps pressing exactly where you are least able to bear it, and the ordinary defences stop holding. The temptation is to fight — to force a resolution, to overpower the feeling, to find someone responsible — and struggle of that kind against this planet only deepens the anguish. What actually helps is admitting the size of what has been carried. That is humiliating, and it is what turns a wound managed privately into something that can eventually be put to use.
chiron-trine-pluto: The old damage can be examined at depth without a crisis to make you do it. What was hidden becomes legible, and the understanding available is thorough rather than glancing: where the injury came from, what it has shaped, and what it has genuinely taught. That combination makes this a good period for serious work in the exact territory where you were hurt, professionally or otherwise, because you can do it without being governed by it. Chiron does not close; what alters here is how much of you it runs.
chiron-opposition-pluto: You meet the injury at full depth and from outside. Someone or something arrives that will not let the old arrangement continue, and the pressure lands squarely on what you have spent years protecting. Power is usually the medium — an imbalance, a dependency, somebody in a position to hurt you where it counts. The first response is to fight, and fighting deepens it. What eventually works is looking at what the wound has been doing in your dealings with people, including what it has been earning you. That is unwelcome, and it is the whole content of the transit.
chiron-conjunction-node: Chiron crosses the axis of your own direction, and the two have more to do with each other than is obvious: very often the work you are here to do runs directly through the place where you were damaged. What surfaces now is that connection. The competence you already have is not what is wanted; what is wanted is the thing you understand because it cost you something. That is an uncomfortable qualification and it is the genuine one. Notice what you are being asked for, and notice how closely it resembles what you have been avoiding.
chiron-sextile-node: A mild, workable contact between the old injury and the line of your own development. An opening appears in which your particular experience turns out to be exactly what some situation requires — a person who needs it, a piece of work that fits, a conversation that goes somewhere useful. Nothing insists, and it is easy to let pass on the grounds that it does not look like an opportunity. What is available briefly is the sense that the injury is not merely a cost. It is also, awkwardly, a qualification.
chiron-square-node: The wound and the direction pull against each other. What you are meant to be developing runs straight through the territory where you were hurt, and everything in you would prefer a different route — so the friction arrives as avoidance dressed up as good sense, or as a situation that will not let you take the easier road. The practised competence at the other end of this axis is genuinely more comfortable and genuinely not what is being asked for. Notice where you are reaching for it, and notice what you are stepping around to do so.
chiron-trine-node: The old damage and your own direction sit in agreement, which does not happen often and makes the connection unusually easy to see: the thing you understand because it cost you something is also the thing you are for. Nothing is pressing and nothing is being demanded, so this is a good stretch for acting on that quietly — taking on work in that territory, saying something you normally route around, being useful to someone in the same difficulty. What is understood here tends to hold, having been arrived at without duress.
chiron-opposition-node: You meet the injury at the accomplished end of your own axis. What you already do well turns out to be built, at least partly, on managing the wound — the competence and the defence are the same structure, and that becomes visible now, usually through somebody who reflects it back. The recognition is unwelcome. It is also the point at which a talent can stop being a way of not feeling something and start being something you actually chose. Nothing here requires you to give up the skill; only to notice what it has been doing.
chiron-conjunction-chiron: Your Chiron return, or one of the harder crossings on the way to it. The injury is not merely touched but revisited at its own degree, and what surfaces is the whole history of it — how long it has been carried, what has been built around it, and what it has made possible as well as what it has cost. Chiron's myth ends with the centaur trading his immortality to release Prometheus: the wound was never healed, and it was eventually exchanged for something. This is the angle at which that exchange becomes thinkable.
chiron-sextile-chiron: A mild point in your own Chiron cycle, offering a look at the injury without much pressure attached. What is available is perspective: where you were at the last hard crossing, what has actually changed since, and what has merely been rearranged. Nothing insists on the review, which is why it usually does not happen. The wound is legible now and comparatively quiet, and something can be done about it cheaply — a conversation, a piece of work, a limit acknowledged — that would cost a great deal more at a harder angle.
chiron-square-chiron: A crisis point in your own Chiron cycle, and the wound is being tested rather than merely felt. What you have built around it comes under pressure: the accommodations, the explanations, the arrangements that let you go on without addressing it. Some of them will not hold. That is uncomfortable and it is how the cycle works — Chiron's crossings ask, at intervals, whether the injury is still running you or whether you have begun to make something of it. The honest answer is usually mixed. Take the pressure as a question rather than a punishment.
chiron-trine-chiron: An easy point in your own Chiron cycle, and one of the few from which the whole shape can be seen without pain distorting the view. You can look back at the earlier crossings and see what has actually changed, what has been genuinely made of the injury and what is still being managed. Nothing demands anything. Because of that, this is unusually good ground for consolidating — putting the understanding to work, taking on something in that territory, saying the thing to somebody who would benefit from hearing it.
chiron-opposition-chiron: The furthest point of your own Chiron cycle, and the injury stands directly opposite you where it can be seen whole. Usually it arrives through other people: someone reflects the wound back at full size, or a situation makes it impossible to keep managing privately. This falls in the middle years for most people and belongs with the other crossings of that period — a reckoning with what has actually been made of a life. The question is not whether the thing has healed. It is what it has been converted into.
chiron-conjunction-mc: Chiron reaches the highest point of your chart and the wound becomes public. Something exposes it in the place where you are seen — a role you cannot occupy without it showing, a limitation that becomes visible to people whose opinion matters, sometimes a piece of work that only your own experience made possible. This is a characteristic angle for the injury and the vocation turning out to be the same thing, which is Chiron's whole proposition: the centaur could not cure himself and taught the physicians.
chiron-sextile-mc: A workable, undramatic contact between the old injury and your standing in the world. Usually it arrives as an opportunity in the territory your history qualifies you for — a piece of work, a request, a role that fits precisely because of what you have been through. Nothing insists on it, and it may not look like an opportunity at all, which is why it often goes past unremarked. What is briefly available is the sense that the injury has some public use, and that using it need not cost you anything.
chiron-square-mc: Something presses on the wound where it touches your work and your standing. Often it takes the form of not being able to occupy your own position — a competence that deserts you at the wrong moment, a comparison you cannot stop making, a limitation exposed in front of people whose regard you wanted. The reaction will outrun the occasion. Both denial and collapse are available and neither is useful. What is being asked is whether the thing can be made part of what you do rather than the reason you cannot do it.
chiron-trine-mc: A rare interval in which the old damage and your public life are on speaking terms. Nothing is pressing on the injury and you can see how it has actually shaped what you do — including the parts where it has made you good at something. That makes this a good period for taking on work in that exact territory, or for saying something publicly you would normally keep private. Chiron does not heal; it becomes usable, and this is the angle at which the conversion costs least and holds longest.
chiron-opposition-mc: Chiron at the foot of your chart, where the wound belongs to the private ground rather than the public one. What surfaces is early and familial: the injury as it was originally made, in the home you came from, before there was any position in the world to defend. Something in your domestic life touches it, or someone close carries it visibly. The public half of your life may have to give way for a while to let this be attended to. It is not a retreat. It is where the foundations get repaired.
